thesis.claim: A world that cannot break still stops improving. In B2 the brains of iteration 2,000 hold between 45% and 55% of a contested world against those of iteration 500, in the median world of ten; and taking the random inputs away does not change that.
thesis.why: In every pilot the cross-time tournament of Chapter 49 flattened within a few hundred iterations: the baseline at +320 to +345 from iteration 200, a B2-like world at +160 to +170 from 200 to 1,000, one with 30% kept at home at +162 to +180 from 50 to 800. Redrawing an evolved agent's random inputs changed 25–58% of its stakes, its neighbour's state 4–23%, its own 2–7%: what evolution found is a way to be unpredictable, which is the best play in a Colonel Blotto contest and cannot be bettered. Without random inputs a pilot flattened all the same (+141 to +188 from 50 to 1,000).
thesis.confirm: In the median world of the ten B2 worlds, and again of the ten without random inputs, the score of iteration 2,000 against iteration 500 — the mean of its two contests — lies between 0.45 and 0.55.
thesis.refute: Above 0.55 in either condition's median world: evolution in that world does not stop by iteration 500.
